title: OSD device descriptor 0.5
description: How a synthesizer, drum machine, controller or music software speaks MIDI or OSC: its identity, controls, messages, programs and drum sounds, with where each piece of data comes from. One file per device and source; a firmware with its own MIDI is its own file. Fields starting with _ are notes for people.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

capabilities.description: What a reader needs beyond the declarative fields. A closed list, today lua (a Lua expression or script). The reader derives the list from the fields present and refuses a declared list that differs; decode lua requires lua.

midi_of.description: The descriptor whose MIDI this firmware answers to unchanged (its id, maker/file without .json): this file then only says what differs.

loads_sounds_of.description: Devices (their address prefix without /) whose sounds this one loads as they are.

selects.description: What a program change selects: the sound kind's list, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as a plain recall).

requires.description: Settings on the device needed first, as its manual names them.

after.description: Messages sent after a recall (before it for before); with program_change false, before and after recall alone.

recall_script.description: A Lua script that writes the recall itself, in place of before, the bank select, the program change and after: it reads ctx (channel, dev, family, member, bank, bank_name, msb, lsb, program, index, number) and returns the messages, a list of lists of bytes. Requires the lua capability.

script.description: A Lua script that writes the request that reads a sound back: it reads ctx like recall_script and returns one list of bytes. Requires the lua capability.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

dump.description: How the current sound is taken from it.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

programs.description: Its programs and banks: how to select one, how they are numbered, how a sound is taken from it.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sysex.description: The bytes every SysEx message of the device starts and ends with.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

cc_params.description: Controls set by Control Change, 14-bit CC pairs, NRPN or RPN.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

params.description: Parameters read and written by SysEx through one shared message shape.

commands.description: Named messages: SysEx utilities, or OSC messages of a software.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

triggers.description: Drum and sample sounds fired by a note.

note_offset.description: Added to every note number sent.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

midi_out.description: Playing it: notes, pitch bend, aftertouch, program change.

midi_in.description: osc-bridge extension: the MIDI messages the device sends while played and that are reported, each at the OSC address the specification fixes, under the device's prefix; what follows the space are the OSC arguments, in this order. note_on: /note/on {note} {velocity} {channel}. note_off: /note/off {note} {velocity} {channel}. cc: /cc/{num} {value} {channel}. pitchbend: /pitchbend {value_u14} {channel}. aftertouch: /aftertouch {value} {channel}. poly_aftertouch: /poly_aftertouch {note} {value} {channel}. program_change: /program_change {program} {channel}. An empty list reports nothing.

replies.description: Messages the device answers or sends by itself, recognised.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

subscriptions.description: OSC messages a software needs at start to report its changes.

osc.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix.

script.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua script that builds the message.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

custom_commands.description: osc-bridge extension: addresses handled by a script only.

_sources.description: Where the data comes from, with its credit, licence and the firmware it documents.

capture_segment.description: A capture in an address: the part of the address that takes the value of the field of this name.

segments.description: An address with captures: the concatenation of its segments, never split on a slash. At least one capture, at most 16 segments; an address without capture is a string.

allOf.$comment: two captures side by side are ambiguous where an address is recognised: none of the 15 pairs of neighbours (the bound is 16 segments) is two objects

emitted_address.description: An address emitted: a string without brace, or an array of segments (a string without brace or a capture); captures may sit side by side.

recognised_address.description: An address recognised: a string without brace, or an array of segments with no two captures side by side.

command_address.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix: a string starting with / and without brace, or segments whose first is a string starting with /.

oneOf.description: The value of an argument of the command.

osc_value.description: An OSC argument: a JSON literal, {"arg": name} (an argument of the command) or {"capture": name} (a field captured in the message).

frame_part.description: An element of a frame that is not a byte: an object of one key of its nature, with the keys that qualify it.

oneOf.title: arg
oneOf.description: An argument of the command, with its encoding, or an offset added to a 7-bit argument (the sum wraps on 7 bits).

oneOf.title: device_id
oneOf.description: The device id, by the rule of identity.device_id with its default value.

oneOf.title: identity
oneOf.description: The bytes of the model's family or member: all of them, or the one at index.

oneOf.title: checksum
oneOf.description: The checksum of the bytes written from offset from (F0 is 0), on length bytes when given: twos7 is Roland's two's complement, sum7 Waldorf's sum, xor7 Fractal's xor, each on 7 bits.

frame_token.description: An element of a message sent: a byte, or an object of one key of its nature (arg, device_id, identity, checksum).

oneOf.title: capture
oneOf.description: Where a recognised message is read: the value is kept under this name.

recognised_frame_token.description: An element of a message recognised: a byte, the word any (any byte), a capture, or an object of one key of its nature (arg, device_id, identity, checksum).

expr.description: A value computed from the arguments, a byte of MIDI data from 0 to 127 as the engine bounds it: add, sub and mul give their result bounded to 0..127; gt, lt, eq and ne give 0 or 1; if gives its second operand when the first is not 0, else its third.

name.description: The model's name, as its maker writes it.

revision.description: The version this file describes (firmware or document).

manufacturer_id.description: The maker's SysEx id: one byte, or three starting with 0.

rate_limit_hz.description: Most messages a second the device takes; 0: no limit known.

transport.description: How a software is reached (OSC host and ports).

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

profile.description: A maker profile this extends (maker or maker/family).

request.description: The identify request, when not the Universal Identity Request (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7); its elements may take the device's own values (an identity object).

to.description: Where the request goes: every_port (default), or named_ports, only the ports whose name matches ports (for a message other devices might misread).

script.description: A Lua script that says whether a reply is this device's, for what reply cannot say: it reads reply (the bytes, from 1) and returns true or false; with reply, both must hold. Requires the lua capability.

reply.description: The start of the reply, element by element: a byte, any, a capture, or an object of its nature.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

decode.description: How the bytes read as a version. A closed list, with no extension: raw_bytes, json (needs field), korg_minor_major, yamaha_tenths, ascii, lua (needs script).

field.description: With decode json: the reply from the offset in at to F7 is a JSON object, and the version is this key's text.

script.description: With decode lua: the script that reads the version from the reply.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

firmware.description: Where the reply carries the firmware version, and how to read it.

ports.description: Its port names, for a device that does not answer.

usb.description: Its USB identities (one per model version or mode): the strongest sign of which model is plugged in, read by a native program (a web browser does not see it).

identity.description: How to recognise the device and its firmware: its answer to an identify request, its port names, its USB identity, what it sends by itself. The controls it sends when its knobs are turned are its cc_params and params.

selects.description: What a bank selects: the sound kind's list, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as a plain recall).

transform.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua expression applied to the value.
